Verbatim: 'Hydrocephalus was not reported during the tofersen CDP so far. However, hydrocephalus has been reported with intrathecally administered ASOs (nusinersen and tominersen) and the risk of hydrocephalus should be further followed.' And: 'hydrocephalus has been reported with nusinersen and a case of hydrocephalus secondary to a sterile meningitis induced by the intrathecally administered ASO tominersen has been reported in literature. Although no events of hydrocephalus were reported in the CDP so far, this risk cannot be excluded for tofersen and should be followed further.'    2025 (cut 15 Jul 2022) reports a range of 18-28.5 cmH2O across 3 participants. Different data cuts over
   overlapping but non-identical case sets - a window difference, not a contradiction. Noted on m89 and m98.
4. Tofersen papilloedema denominator. The US label says "Four patients developed elevated intracranial pressure
   and/or papilledema"; the EMA EPAR Table 37 gives 7/147 (4.8%) for the composite term. The label counts only
   the SERIOUS events (EPAR Table 38: 3 ICP-increased + 1 papilloedema = 4). Both are right; they count
   different things. This is exactly the kind of beyond-label detail this lane was asked to add.

=== THINGS I SUSPECT BUT COULD NOT CONFIRM ===
- That a preclinical NHP or rodent hydrocephalus/ventriculomegaly signal exists in sponsor toxicology packages.
  I could not confirm one. See the honest assessment below.
- That the tominersen ventricular signal is dose-frequency- rather than dose-amount-driven. Every tominersen
  arm in every trial used 120 mg; only the interval varied (Q4W/Q8W/Q16W), and the signal orders monotonically
  with frequency in three independent studies. But the Phase I/IIa dose ladder (10-120 mg at a fixed 4-weekly
  interval, m65-m74) also shows a monotonic ventricular-volume gradient, so amount matters too. The two cannot
  be separated with the available public data.
- Whether nusinersen actually causes hydrocephalus at all, as opposed to unmasking it. See below.

=== HOW WELL-SOURCED IS THIS ENDPOINT REALLY? AN HONEST ASSESSMENT ===
Do not let the row count mislead anyone. The 100 rows are unevenly strong, and the documentation should say so.

STRONG (placebo- or dose-controlled, public-domain, quantitative):
- Tominersen ventricular volume. This is the best evidence in the endpoint by a wide margin. GENERATION HD1
  gives a placebo-controlled LS-mean ventricular volume change at 13 weeks (m38, m39). The Phase I/IIa study
  gives a five-dose ladder with a concurrent placebo arm and absolute ventricular volumes in mL at two
  timepoints (m65-m74). The OLE gives a 46% versus 19% separation by dosing frequency (m52, m53). All of it is
  ClinicalTrials.gov posted results, i.e. public domain and reproducible by anyone.
- Tominersen serious hydrocephalus, placebo-controlled: 2/263 on Q8W versus 0/264 on Q16W and 0/264 on placebo
  (m34-m37). Concordant across three further studies.
- Tofersen papilloedema / raised ICP with a placebo comparator and per-group denominators (m86-m96), plus an
  explicit EMA statement that hydrocephalus was NOT observed (m90).

MODERATE (real numbers, but confounded, uncontrolled, or from a non-peer-reviewed source):
- The five nusinersen DHPC cases (m1-m6). These are spontaneous post-marketing reports with clinical detail but
  no denominator that matches the numerator, and no control group of any kind.
- The DEVOTE dose comparison (m10-m15). Directionally the best nusinersen evidence, but the events are n=1 and
  n=2 against denominators of 50, 16 and 40. Suggestive, not demonstrative.
- The CHDI slides (m80-m84). Genuinely unique data - the 4/636 programme-wide denominator and the 16
  asymptomatic radiographic cases appear nowhere else I could find - but they are sponsor conference slides
  labelled "preliminary" and "subject to change", and are marked redistribution=verify for that reason.

WEAK OR ABSENT:
- PRECLINICAL EVIDENCE IS ESSENTIALLY ABSENT, AND THIS IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST GAP. I searched PubMed
  systematically (oligonucleotide x hydrocephalus x monkey/mouse/rat; ASO x ventriculomegaly; ICV ASO x
  ventriculomegaly), read the largest published NHP intrathecal-ASO safety survey (1,016 monkeys, 28 studies),
  read a full GLP NHP tox study, and searched both the Spinraza and Qalsody EPAR nonclinical sections. I found
  NO published animal study in which an oligonucleotide CAUSED hydrocephalus or ventricular enlargement. The
  Spinraza EPAR (117 pages) contains ZERO occurrences of "ventric", "hydroceph", "ependym" or "brain weight" -
  the nonclinical package appears not to have examined ventricular size at all, which is very likely why the
  signal only emerged post-marketing. The one preclinical row in this lane (m100) is negative evidence of the
  weakest kind: absence of hydrocephalus from a list of five CLINICAL NEUROLOGICAL SIGN categories, in studies
  that did not image ventricles. The one other preclinical row (m99) is an oligonucleotide that PREVENTS
  hydrocephalus, from an abstract. THE DATASET MUST NOT CLAIM PRECLINICAL COVERAGE OF THIS ENDPOINT.
- NO in vitro human-based system (iPSC neuron, organoid, ependymal or choroid-plexus model) contributes a
  single row. NCATS specifically wants those. For hydrocephalus there is nothing to extract - the endpoint is
  intrinsically organ-level, and no one appears to have built an in vitro CSF-dynamics model for oligo tox.
- NO pharmacovigilance disproportionality statistic (ROR/PRR/IC) for hydrocephalus was found. I checked five
  FAERS/EudraVigilance/VigiBase studies of nusinersen and SMA therapies. The EudraVigilance analysis
  (PMC12072878, 3,196 nusinersen ICSRs to 31 Dec 2024) reports NO hydrocephalus, ventriculomegaly, raised-ICP
  or papilloedema term at all; the FAERS studies surface "CSF pressure increased" and "CSF protein increased"
  but not hydrocephalus. So the signal, while real in case reports and regulatory documents, is NOT large
  enough to surface in published disproportionality analyses. That is worth saying out loud.

THE CAUSALITY PROBLEM FOR NUSINERSEN, WHICH THE DOCUMENTATION SHOULD STATE PLAINLY:
Two independent lines of evidence argue that a substantial part of the nusinersen hydrocephalus signal is
attributable to SMA itself rather than to the drug. (1) A matched-cohort US EHR study covering the PRE-
nusinersen era (Optum, 5,354 SMA cases versus 5,354 matched controls, Orphanet J Rare Dis 2021, PMC8105953,
Table 2) found hydrocephalus incidence of 15.5 versus 3.3 per 100,000 person-months, IRR 4.7 (95% CI 2.4-10.2)
- SMA carries a roughly fourfold to fivefold baseline hydrocephalus risk with no drug involved. (2) Becker 2021
found lumbar puncture opening pressure above 20 cmH2O in most of a 34-patient nusinersen cohort, including two
patients whose pressure was already raised BEFORE treatment started, and concluded that raised opening pressure
may be a feature of SMA. Add to this that the sham-controlled pivotal trials ENDEAR and CHERISH recorded no
hydrocephalus in either arm (m20, m21), and hydrocephalus remains an important POTENTIAL risk in the EU RMP,
not an important identified risk (EMA/CHMP/379593/2025). I have NOT filed the Optum study as a measurement row
because it involves no oligonucleotide exposure and therefore has no place in an oligo x dose x readout grain;
it is carried in the notes of m1 and here. It should nonetheless be cited wherever the nusinersen rows are
discussed.
By contrast the tominersen signal is much harder to explain away: it is placebo-controlled, dose- and
frequency-ordered, quantitative on imaging, and accompanied by a formal lumbar infusion study demonstrating
increased resistance to CSF outflow in the shunted case (m57). If the dataset is going to make one claim about
this endpoint, it should be about tominersen, not nusinersen.
A third pattern worth surfacing: raised intracranial pressure and hydrocephalus DISSOCIATE across these three
drugs. Tofersen produces papilloedema and raised ICP (4.8%) with zero hydrocephalus (m90). One nusinersen case
had an opening pressure of 47 cmH2O with severe papilledema and entirely NORMAL ventricles (m29-m31).
Tominersen produces ventriculomegaly and communicating hydrocephalus. Any model trained on this lane should
treat "raised ICP" and "ventriculomegaly" as separate labels, which is why they are separate readout_names here
and why the endpoint_domain=hydrocephalus bucket deliberately spans both.
